The welcome email, before anyone gets it

Rendered from emails/welcome/copy.json on 2026-09-14. Nothing has been sent. The automation is written and switched off. Edit the copy file, run node emails/welcome/build.mjs, and this page rebuilds with it.

FOUNDER COPY · NOT SENT

The letter is the founder’s own, locked on 2026-09-13.

Nobody is mailed until the postal address is set, a real test send has been approved, and the automation is switched on, which are separate decisions. The list at the bottom says where each one stands.

How it renders

The real HTML, in three frames. Scroll inside any of them.

The fourth frame is the real dark treatment with its media query forced on, so it is the same bytes Apple Mail would render rather than a mock-up of them. Gmail is the one thing no preview can show: it ignores that block entirely and runs its own inversion over the light palette, which is what the light palette is chosen to survive.

In an inbox

A subject line is only ever read in a list, beside a sender name, with the preheader trailing off the end of the row. The sender name is the half that usually decides the open.

  1. Suraj from bingd I built bingd. Tell me what you think. — Hit reply and it comes straight to me. recommended
  2. Suraj from bingd Thanks for trying bingd. — Hit reply and it comes straight to me.
  3. Suraj from bingd A note from the person who made bingd. — Hit reply and it comes straight to me.

Suraj from bingd reads as a person. bingd. reads as a service, and this email's whole claim is that a person wrote it.

Subject and preheader

Subject · recommended

I built bingd. Tell me what you think.

It asks a question, which is the one thing a subject line can do that makes replying feel like the obvious response rather than an extra step.

Alternative

Thanks for trying bingd.

Alternative

A note from the person who made bingd.

Preheader · recommended

Hit reply and it comes straight to me.

The grey line after the subject. Second of three places the reply invitation appears before anybody scrolls.

Where every link and instruction goes

A directly deep-linkable   I an instruction inside the app, with no link, whose labels are checked against the app’s source   D not currently practical, and refused by the build.

CardClassDestinationWhat receives it
inviteLink C https://bingd.app/i/{{inviteToken}} /i/* is in appPaths and app/i/[token].tsx receives it. It is the exact URL the app shares: use-recommend.ts builds `https://bingd.app/i/${token}` from create_invite_link's token. Without the app: web/dist/i.html: the invitation page with the install row and 'I already have bingd.'. No token: Tokens are minted lazily, so many new accounts have none. The claim mints the one personal link under create_invite_link's own lock, with no invite_link_creations row and no other side effect. README.md, 'The invite link'.
founderProfile A https://bingd.app/u/saisurajkan /u/* is in appPaths; app/u/[username].tsx renders the profile and FollowControl. Without the app: web/dist/u.html resolves the display name and avatar and offers the install row plus Open in bingd.
Group Picks label Rendered by app/(tabs)/recommendations.tsx The chip that opens GroupPicksSheet. Nothing in the app is called Group Watch.
For you label Rendered by app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx The tab's title, lower-case y.

Invite friends and Group Picks have no link that lands on them: one lives on the Profile tab, the other is a chip on the For you tab with no route. So their cards say where to tap and carry no button, rather than a button that opens the wrong screen.

Plain text

Generated from the same copy, never hand-maintained. A message with no text part is a spam signal, and a hand-written one stops matching the HTML on the second edit. 

{{greeting}}

Thanks for giving bingd a shot. I built it because the usual 1–5 star
ratings never really felt like they captured the experience of watching
a good movie or TV show.

Here are a few of my favorite ways to use the app:

Post-watch Ranking: Instead of picking a number, compare titles
head-to-head and bingd builds your ranked list. That list keeps evolving
as you discover new favorites (Avengers: Doomsday anyone?).

Pre-vetted Watchlist: My favorite part of the feed is not just seeing
what my friends are watching. It's putting those titles in my watchlist
and then teasing them about their taste later (The Emoji Movie,
really?).

Smooth Planning: The Group Picks feature (under For you) generates
recommendations across multiple bingd users when you're struggling to
find a pick before the popcorn runs out. It's a favorite for movie clubs
and couples!

If you want to suggest a new feature, find something confusing, or love
the app and just want to say hi, you can hit reply to this email. It
comes straight to me.

bingd is more fun with friends, so here's your invite link
(https://bingd.app/i/{{inviteToken}}). And if you want to see what I'm
watching, follow me on bingd (https://bingd.app/u/saisurajkan).

Happy binging,
Suraj

bingd is made by Suraj Kandukuri.

Still yours to decide

  1. Pick the subject. Three candidates are shown as inbox rows above. subject.chosen is "I built bingd. Tell me what you think.".
  2. Postal address. Not set, so the worker refuses the cohort. A commercial email carries a physical mailing address; there is no company, so it is one you are willing to publish, usually a PO box or a virtual mailbox.
  3. Send from bingd.app. Replies go to suraj@bingd.app. Sending as that address needs bingd.app added and verified in Resend (DKIM, the send subdomain, DMARC). Until then a test send uses --from "Suraj from bingd <suraj@auth.bingd.app>".
  4. A Resend key of its own. Sending access, restricted to bingd.app. Never the key named Supabase: that one relays every sign-in code.

Not sent to anybody. Automation written and disabled. One email, one copy file, and every link and instruction in it checked against the app.
